plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own. Bidding higher risks winning at a price above my value (negative profit), while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities where the second-highest bid is between my bid and value. With value $9, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit regardless of competitors' strategies.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, which is strategically equivalent to a Vickrey auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding higher than my value risks overpaying, and bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With my value at $9, I should bid exactly $9 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (winner pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior, since the bid only affects whether I win, not what I pay if I win. Bidding above value risks winning at a loss; bidding below value risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $34 to maximize expected profit.
